rules.description: The `base` collection's `color` branch is a direct 1:1 alias of AppTheme.semanticColors, so the Kotlin accessor is the Figma path with its leading `color/` segment dropped and each remaining segment camelCased.
rules.evidence: themedata/DsThemeColors.kt declares `typealias SemanticColors = com.dexcom.platform.design.foundation.token.base.color.Color` — a direct, un-renamed, un-restructured alias of the generated Base.Color class — and AppTheme.kt's `semanticColors` property returns exactly that type. Verified against the generated Color.kt's nested classes (Surface -> Action -> Primary -> default matches color/surface/action/primary/default segment for segment).

rules.reason: Only Base.color is a confirmed 1:1 alias of AppTheme.semanticColors. base's other branches (border-width, effect, opacity, radius, scale, apple) have no confirmed wiring: AppTheme.opacity (AppOpacity), AppTheme.shapes (AppShapes) and AppTheme.dimensions (AppDimensions) are hand-authored data classes in themedata/ with their own field names (AppShapes.radius40, AppDimensions.extraSmall, ...) and hardcoded literal Dp/Float defaults — not typealiases, not generated from Base, and not a 1:1 rename of any Base.* path. Guessing here would very likely be wrong.

Collections other than `base` (components, layout, primitives, typography) have not been investigated for Kotlin wiring — color was the explicit priority. Their Figma-side `codeSyntax` hints are carried in the Token IR under `hints.codeSyntax` for humans and coding agents, but are deliberately NOT used to derive a symbol: the platform is moving to a Styles API that will supply the real symbols.
